You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The policy rate sits at +3 relative to its 3-year average, having risen sharply over both the last 3 and 12 months, so the Fed has been hiking. Core CPI is high while headline CPI is lower. Industrial production is very weak and the unemployment rate is low relative to its own history. Credit spreads are wide, VIX is elevated, and equities are down with large drawdowns. Treasuries are rallying.

A policy rate that has risen 3 SD in 3 months suggests it moved from near zero to well above it, which fits the 2022 hiking cycle. But in 2022 the 10-year yield was rising, whereas here it is -1.0 with a falling 3-month change. A window in which the 12m change in the policy rate is also +3 and the rate is far above its 36-month average could be late 2022 or early 2023.

Other candidates:
- Dec 2018: the rate had risen steadily, so its 3-year z-score would not be +3 on a 3-month change.
- Mar 2023: the SVB crisis pushed the VIX up, credit spreads widened, and Treasuries rallied (7-10y +2.0 over 1 month). The 2-year yield z of +1.5 with a 0 3-month change fits. The 10y-2y spread was deeply inverted. Equities were down 12m, which fits March 2023 (S&P 12m roughly -9%). Core CPI at +2.5 fits. Payrolls were still strong. Industrial production -2.5 is odd, but it could be a reading artifact.

However, in March 2023 the S&P gained over 1 month (+3.7%), whereas here it is -2.0. Equity 1m, 3m, 6m and 12m are all negative, which points more to September or October 2022. Treasuries were not rallying then, though. Another fit is late 2008, but the policy rate was falling then.

A candidate that fits better is Oct 2023: equities fell, but Treasuries fell too, and 12m equity was positive. So that does not work.

Headline CPI's 3m change is +1.5, which suggests rising inflation. That does not fit March 2023, when inflation was falling. It could fit the early-2022 rise, but then the policy rate would not be +3.

A possibility is 2007, since the 36-month window then covers the 2004-2006 hiking cycle. The policy rate would be at a high z-score, but a +3 change over 12 months wouldn't fit.

Another is the Covid period. Policy rate z +3 with a 3m change of +3 is not consistent with 2020, when rates were cut.

I'll settle on Mar 2023 with low confidence. The IP weakness could come from a different pattern, and 1m Treasury +2.0 with VIX up fits the SVB episode.
